hints: At steady speed $50\text{ m s}^{-1}$, driving force equals resistance: $\frac{62500}{50} = k(50^2)$, and solve for $k$.
At speed $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$, driving force is $D = \frac{62500}{25} = 2500\text{ N}$ and resistance is $R = 0.5(25^2) = 312.5\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law: $D - R = ma \implies 2500 - 312.5 = 2500a$ and evaluate $a$.
walkthrough:
At steady speed $v = 50\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on the level road, driving force balances resistance:
$$D = R \implies \frac{P}{v} = kv^2 \implies \frac{62500}{50} = k(50^2)$$
$$1250 = 2500k \implies k = \frac{1250}{2500} = 0.5$$

When the speed is $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$, calculate the driving force and resistance:
$$D = \frac{62500}{25} = 2500\text{ N}$$
$$R = kv^2 = 0.5(25^2) = 0.5(625) = 312.5\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law with mass $m = 2500\text{ kg}$:
$$D - R = ma \implies 2500 - 312.5 = 2500a$$
$$2187.5 = 2500a \implies a = \frac{2187.5}{2500} = 0.875\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the resistance constant $k$.
Given power $P = 62.5\text{ kW} = 62500\text{ W}$. At steady speed $v = 50\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on a level road, acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), so the driving force $D$ equals the resistance force $R$:
$$D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{62500}{50} = 1250\text{ N}$$
$$R = kv^2 = k(50^2) = 2500k$$
Equating driving force and resistance:
$$1250 = 2500k$$
$$k = \frac{1250}{2500} = 0.5$$

Step 2: Acceleration when speed is $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
Driving force from constant engine power:
$$D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{62500}{25} = 2500\text{ N}$$
Resistance force with $k = 0.5$:
$$R = kv^2 = 0.5(25^2) = 0.5(625) = 312.5\text{ N}$$

hints: Set up Newton's second law at speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with acceleration $5a$: $\frac{62500}{20} - 0.5(20^2) - 2500g \sin \theta = 2500(5a)$.
Set up Newton's second law at speed $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with acceleration $a$: $\frac{62500}{30} - 0.5(30^2) - 2500g \sin \theta = 2500a$.
Subtract the second equation from the first to eliminate $\sin \theta$ and solve for $a$, then substitute $a$ back to find $\theta$.
walkthrough:
Write Newton's second law at speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with acceleration $5a$:
$$\frac{62500}{20} - 0.5(20^2) - 2500g \sin \theta = 2500(5a)$$
$$3125 - 200 - 25000 \sin \theta = 12500a \implies 2925 - 25000 \sin \theta = 12500a$$

Write Newton's second law at speed $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with acceleration $a$:
$$\frac{62500}{30} - 0.5(30^2) - 2500g \sin \theta = 2500a$$
$$\frac{6250}{3} - 450 - 25000 \sin \theta = 2500a \implies \frac{4900}{3} - 25000 \sin \theta = 2500a$$

Subtract the two equations to eliminate $25000 \sin \theta$:
$$2925 - \frac{4900}{3} = 12500a - 2500a = 10000a$$
$$\frac{8775 - 4900}{3} = \frac{3875}{3} = 10000a \implies a = \frac{3875}{30000} = \frac{31}{240} \approx 0.129\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = \frac{31}{240}$ to determine the incline angle $\theta$:
$$25000 \sin \theta = \frac{4900}{3} - 2500\left(\frac{31}{240}\right) = \frac{4900}{3} - \frac{3875}{12} = \frac{15725}{12} \approx 1310.42$$
$$\sin \theta = \frac{15725}{300000} \approx 0.052417 \implies \theta = \arcsin(0.052417) \approx 3.00^\circ$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Set up equation of motion at $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Driving force: $D_1 = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{62500}{20} = 3125\text{ N}$.
Resistance force: $R_1 = 0.5(20^2) = 0.5(400) = 200\text{ N}$.
Component of weight down the slope: $W_{\parallel} = mg \sin \theta = 2500(10)\sin \theta = 25000 \sin \theta$.
Acceleration is $5a$:
$$D_1 - R_1 - mg \sin \theta = m(5a)$$
$$3125 - 200 - 25000 \sin \theta = 2500(5a)$$
$$2925 - 25000 \sin \theta = 12500a \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Step 2: Set up equation of motion at $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Driving force: $D_2 = \frac{62500}{30} = \frac{6250}{3} = 2083.33\text{ N}$.
Resistance force: $R_2 = 0.5(30^2) = 0.5(900) = 450\text{ N}$.
Acceleration is $a$:
$$D_2 - R_2 - mg \sin \theta = ma$$
$$\frac{6250}{3} - 450 - 25000 \sin \theta = 2500a$$
$$\frac{4900}{3} - 25000 \sin \theta = 2500a \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Step 3: Eliminate $\sin \theta$ by subtracting Equation 2 from Equation 1:
$$\left(2925 - \frac{4900}{3}\right) = 12500a - 2500a$$
$$\frac{8775 - 4900}{3} = 10000a$$
$$\frac{3875}{3} = 10000a$$
$$a = \frac{3875}{30000} = \frac{31}{240} \approx 0.129167\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.129\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Step 4: Solve for the incline angle $\theta$ using Equation 2:
$$25000 \sin \theta = \frac{4900}{3} - 2500\left(\frac{31}{240}\right)$$
$$25000 \sin \theta = \frac{4900}{3} - \frac{3875}{12} = \frac{19600 - 3875}{12} = \frac{15725}{12} \approx 1310.4167$$
$$\sin \theta = \frac{15725}{12 \times 25000} = \frac{15725}{300000} \approx 0.0524167$$
$$\theta = \arcsin(0.0524167) \approx 3.0039^\circ \approx 3.00^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Sets up four-term N2L equations at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, solves simultaneously to obtain $a = 0.129\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $\theta = 3.00^\circ$.
